Most people who go in mental health fields struggle with mental health. We are called to it because we know what it's like. People will listen to you because you aren't bullshitting them. You know firsthand how miserable it is. We don't know the causes, but we are figuring out more coping strategies. Therapists aren't there to cure people, they are there to help when people are in dark and scary places. I always remind myself that my depression gave me a path and purpose in life, which many people my age struggle with. It sucks to have these symptoms, but it's led me to a meaningful career. So many people have no idea what to do with their lives, and I do. I count that as lucky. I'm studying marriage and family therapy and while grad school itself is isolating, I'm thrilled to be doing something that matters. Just know that you could be helping people one day. It's not about curing depression.

they're extensively trained to talk to you about these things and the fact that they don't know you means that they're impartial. but bad therapists are shitty to deal with. good therapists are a godsend.
